messages:
Mira Chen: Heads-up — seeing steady KV cache growth on Dedicated pools (a100-dedicated-us-west). After long-context runs (8k tokens) memory slowly climbs even with identical request mix. Not repro on Hosted; Private (onprem A100) shows similar growth but with more fragmentation.

Mira Chen: Quick profile snapshot:
```text
sample: dedicated/usw-a100-1 - 6h run - rss 89GB, kv-resident 72GB, fragmentation metric 0.27
sample: hosted/eu-standard-3 - 6h run - rss 46GB, kv-resident 40GB, fragmentation 0.12
sample: private/onprem-rack3 - 6h run - rss 85GB, kv-resident 68GB, fragmentation 0.31
flame: internal link /prof/3612345 (kv hotspots: pagebackfill, slab-sweep)
kernel: dedicated nodes running 5.15.x, hosted on 6.1.x, private on 5.15-custom
batching: continuous batching enabled, window=25ms on all clusters
```

Sanjay Kapoor: Are the Dedicated boxes using jumbo frames/MTU 9000? We had a previous case where RDMA/NVLink tuning changed pagewalk timing and increased pagefault storms.

Mira Chen: Good call — Dedicated is configured with MTU 9000; Hosted is 1500; Private is mixed (some racks 9000, some 1500). I suspect network NIC coalescing + kernel/pagecache behavior interacting with our KV pager.

Eli Baxter: Quick note: recent kernel selector change picks a fallback kernel path when numa balancing heuristics trip. That fallback disables async page reclaim optimizations we rely on. If dedicated nodes stuck on fallback path, steady-state will be worse.

Eli Baxter: Repro command I used:
```bash
python -m perf.run_workload --model x --ctx 8192 --rate 12 --duration 6h 
# attach /proc/vmstat and slabinfo sampling every 30s
```
Output snippet: "pgmajfault" spikes correlated with kv-slab fragmentation climbs.

Paola Rivera: On Private we've seen compaction disabled in our custom kernel (CONFIG_COMPACTION=n). That could explain higher fragmentation there. Can infra confirm if Dedicated kernel has CONFIG_COMPACTION=y?

infra-bot: deploy-check: nodes/a100-dedicated-us-west kernel-config: CONFIG_COMPACTION=y, THP=enabled, transparent_hugepage=always

Sanjay Kapoor: If Dedicated has THP enabled + MTU 9000 maybe hugepage allocation/defrag interacts with our jemalloc arena layout. Try forcing THP=deferred on a canary host and see if kv fragmentation slope improves. Also turn on per-tenant slab sampling (we have a toggle in runtime flags).

Mira Chen: Plan: 1) spin a canary on dedicated with THP=deferred and mtu=1500, 2) enable per-tenant slab sampling and flamegraphs, 3) run same workload and compare kv-resident + frag metric. I'll also try kernel 6.1 build on a dedicated box to isolate selector fallback effect.

Eli Baxter: Also add a run with batching window=5ms vs 25ms. Shorter window reduces co-scheduling and might lower peak slot residency causing less long-lived frames. Put both runs in the same incident ticket so we can correlate.

Paola Rivera: FYI, on Private we need to watch for our GPU scheduler (onprem-sched) that pins frames for host-copy optimization — that was a source of long-lived allocations in a past report. If present, try disabling and compare.

Mira Chen: Thx — I'll run experiments tomorrow and post minimal diffs. If we see frag drop on THP/MTU change then we can standardize Dedicated to match Hosted behavior or add runtime coalescing to mitigate.

Sanjay Kapoor: If canary looks good, let's also try a small change to kernel selector to avoid the fallback path for our common longctx profile (we can gate via runtime feature flag).

Mira Chen: Sounds good. Creating thread in incident board and will paste raw logs + flamegraphs. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ticket created: INF-4821 - kv-cache frag triage (links: /tickets/INF-4821)
